small_guidance:
- The conv (nn.Conv3d on 4×32×32×128×128 with 64 out channels) dominates runtime; tuning the already-fused pool+LSE+ReLU kernel further yields little. If staying small, increase BLOCK_S to 64-128 and num_warps to 4 so each program covers more spatial outputs and amortizes index math, and try channels_last memory layout for the conv input/output to improve coalescing on the C axis.
- Add a tl.maximum(lse, 0.0) fast path that skips the exp/log when row_max < 0 is impossible here, but consider replacing `tl.log(sum_exp) + row_max` with a numerically stable single-pass online LSE to cut register pressure.
large_guidance:
- Replace nn.Conv3d with a custom Triton implicit-GEMM conv3d kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), gather the 3×3×3×IC window implicitly, accumulate into a BLOCK_M×BLOCK_N tile, and fuse the bias add directly in the epilogue. This is the only path to meaningful speedup since conv is >90% of runtime.
- Fuse the 2×2×2 maxpool, channel-wise logsumexp, and ReLU into the conv epilogue: have the conv kernel emit output in pool-tile granularity (each program produces a 2×2×2 spatial block per channel), keep the 8 conv outputs in registers, and reduce them in-place before writing — eliminating the entire intermediate (N, 64, 32, 128, 128) tensor write/read.
- Use channels_last (NDHWC) layout end-to-end so the GEMM-K dimension (IC × kd × kh × kw) is contiguous and the channel reduction for LSE coalesces; autotune BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K around 64/64/32 with num_warps∈{4,8}, num_stages∈{2,3}.
